A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–I. The additional page in v3 reflects added administrative text and repagination, with no missing comparison material.

before.justification: v2 reports original unlearning experiments on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, calibration measurements, and human–LLM judge comparisons in Section 6 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 reports the same original model experiments, calibration measurements, human–LLM comparisons, and supplementary analyses in Section 6 and Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix A retain the same confidence-aware graph framework, entropy-filtered subgraph extraction, calibration, and adversarial LLM-judge procedure. The prompts and implementation refinements also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use YAGO3-10 for factual unlearning, MMLU for general knowledge, and BBH for reasoning. The sentence-based and QA-based scenarios and appendix coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 and the supplementary comparisons retain GA, RL, NPO, NegGrad+, and SCRUB in the same configurations, along with the same no-unlearning reference and instance-level evaluation comparison.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices B–D retain the same target models, full/LoRA configurations, 200 target triples, 2,000 neighboring triples, metrics, training budgets, and epoch-selection rule. No experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: The confidence-threshold, forget-set-size, and epoch studies remain unchanged. Calibration checks, judge validation, case studies, local-consistency analyses, and score-distribution analyses in Appendices D–F also match.

E5.justification: Both disclose random seed 42 in Appendix D and three LLM-scoring rounds plus three independent human ratings in Section 6.3. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All main and appendix results match. For example, Table 1 retains instance/proposed UES values of 0.157/0.076 for full-model GA on LLaMA with sentence templates, and Figure 7 retains a human–LLM Pearson correlation of 0.826.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the formal graph and judge setup, Appendix B loss equations, and Appendix G's entropy–probability derivation are unchanged. Mathematical spacing differences do not alter their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claim that conventional evaluations overestimate unlearning effectiveness by overlooking correlated knowledge and confidence.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix I's limitations concerning evaluator ability, incomplete subgraphs, probing inaccuracies, and reference-graph dependence are unchanged. The new JPMorgan disclaimer is institutional boilerplate rather than a scientific qualification.

D1.justification: The code link, prompt templates, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, DeepSpeed/vLLM settings, filtering details, and runtime information are unchanged in the abstract and Appendices A–D.

R1.justification: Section 2's research positioning and all 65 cited works are unchanged. The references are repaginated without additions, removals, or substantive revisions.

P1.justification: v3 adds Mohsen Ghassemi and Vamsi K. Potluru as authors, adds their affiliation and contact details, revises acknowledgments, and inserts a JPMorgan disclaimer. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author block and added disclaimer reflow paragraphs, figure placement, and references. Figures 1–30 and Tables 1–7 retain their content and structure; the appendix contents move from page 14 to page 15.

improvement.justification: v3 updates authorship and acknowledgments and adds an institutional disclaimer, while preserving the scientific arguments, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations. The modest layout changes establish no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
